reference_items.stem:
The graph shows the number of students at each grade in the Pine School.

[Image: Bar graph titled Pine School shows 6 columns labeled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6. X-axis is labeled Grade. Y-axis is labeled Number of Students with values from 0 to 35 and increments at every 5 units.
• Grade 1: value of 20.
• Grade 2: value of 25.
• Grade 3: value of 20.
• Grade 4: value of 25.
• Grade 5: value of 30.
• Grade 6: value of 25.]

In the Pine School there is room in each grade for 30 students. How many more students could be in the school?
reference_items.figure_description:
A vertical bar graph titled "Pine School". The vertical axis is labeled "Number of Students" and is marked with grid lines from 0 to 35 in increments of 5 (0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35). The horizontal axis is labeled "Grade" and has tick marks labeled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. The shaded gray bars have the following heights:
- Grade 1: height 20
- Grade 2: height 25
- Grade 3: height 20
- Grade 4: height 25
- Grade 5: height 30
- Grade 6: height 25

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Ahmed made a survey of the favorite color of the students in 4 classes.

[Image: Four bar graph figures labeled Class 1, Class 2, Class 3, Class 4 with 3 columns labeled Red, Green, and Blue on x-axis. Y-axis with values of 0 to 14 for Class 1 and Class 4 and values of 0 to 15 for Class 2 and Class 3.
• Class 1: Red value of 12, Green value of 10, Blue value of 8.
• Class 2: Red value of 10, Green value of 15, Blue value of 5.
• Class 3: Red value of 5, Green value of 10, Blue value of 15.
• Class 4: Red value of 7, Green value of 10, Blue value of 13.]

In which class do the fewest students choose blue?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four bar graphs arranged in a 2-by-2 grid, each showing student choices for favorite colors (Red, Green, Blue):
- Class 1 (top-left): The vertical axis ranges from 0 to 14 in increments of 2, with grid lines at 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 14. The horizontal axis has three bars: Red is shaded gray with a height of 12; Green is shaded black with a height of 10; Blue is unshaded (white) with a height of 8.
- Class 2 (top-right): The vertical axis ranges from 0 to 15 in increments of 5, with grid lines at 0, 5, 10, and 15. The horizontal axis has three bars: Red is gray with a height of 10; Green is black with a height of 15; Blue is white with a height of 5.
- Class 3 (bottom-left): The vertical axis ranges from 0 to 15 in increments of 5, with grid lines at 0, 5, 10, and 15. The horizontal axis has three bars: Red is gray with a height of 5; Green is black with a height of 10; Blue is white with a height of 15.
- Class 4 (bottom-right): The vertical axis ranges from 0 to 14 in increments of 2, with grid lines at 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 14. The horizontal axis has three bars: Red is gray with a height of 7; Green is black with a height of 10; Blue is white with a height of 13.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
